transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

I’m here because no matter what anyone says, I know some people at work are secretly working together to set me up, and nobody seems to take that seriously. It is incredibly frustrating that everyone just brushes it off as a coincidence when I know exactly what they are trying to do to me.
Besides these concerns about your coworkers, have you also been experiencing significant periods of feeling extremely low, hopeless, or unusually energetic and elated?
No, I haven't really felt that way. My mood is generally fine, it's just that all my stress and focus right now is entirely on what these people at work are trying to do to me.

Have you noticed any other changes, such as hearing voices, feeling like your thoughts are being controlled by others, or experiencing a significant decline in your ability to take care of your daily personal hygiene or work responsibilities?

No, I don't hear any voices or feel like my mind is being controlled, and my life outside of work—like paying my bills on time and hanging out with my brothers—is completely normal. Work has gotten tense with heated staff meetings and my supervisor pulling me aside, but that's only because I'm staying vigilant to protect myself from being set up. I still do my inspections exactly by the book and take care of my responsibilities.
How long have you felt that your coworkers are conspiring against you, and has this belief remained consistent throughout this entire period?

This has been going on for about a year now, starting right after a senior driver publicly challenged me in front of everyone following that bus collision incident. Since then, it’s been completely constant, and I haven't doubted for a second what they are trying to do to me.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with a persistent, non-bizarre delusional belief regarding a conspiracy at work for over a year, in the absence of hallucinations, thought disorder, or significant functional impairment outside of the specific delusional context. The clinical presentation does not meet the criteria for schizophrenia or mood disorders.
